title: Timbuktu
summary: The university city of West Africa, caught between Mali and Songhai.

claims.text: Timbuktu and its University-Mosque of Sankore sit between fading Mali to the west and rising Songhai to the east; Tuareg tribesmen took the city from Mali's king, and Songhai kings now covet it.
Songhai folk are quick to see through mages who use their Arts to hide or to fake the local tongue.

title: Songhai belief and magic
summary: Village spirit-workers of the Songhai lands.

claims.text: Islam is strong among the Songhai, but most still keep the old faith; every village has sorko and witches, and mediums led by a zima, a spiritualist often possessed by powerful spirits.
Mother's milk is held to pass on magical power, and the bonds between mothers, daughters and sisters run deep.

By 1519 more than forty conquered provinces paid tribute to the emperor, who would soon need a Flower War, a battle fought only to take captives for sacrifice, if no new states could be found to conquer.

Quetzalcoatl was said to have gone to seek a bearded, white-skinned man; later priests changed the tale so that the god would return as one, and Cortes' arrival, with strange portents, put the empire's fate in Spanish hands.

title: Ngoma
summary: Wizard-priests of the Zimbabwe plain who interpret the spirits.

claims.text: Ngoma are part priest, part miracle-worker, solving the great riddles of the world to speak for the spirits; their true beginning as a group came with the move to the cities of the plain.
Many study nature for astrology and geomancy, others travel in dreams to far realms, and a few journey across Africa to meet other magi.

title: Lions of Zion
summary: Kabbalist guardians of Israel who call on the angels.

claims.text: The Lions draw secret names of angels and words of Creation from the Torah through Kabbalah, books like the Sepher Yetzirah, numerology and wordplay.
Calling the angels by their true names lets them wield God's power for defence, healing and righteous wrath.
